Russian

[edit]
Russian numbers (edit)
10
 ←  0 1 2  →  10  → 
    Cardinal: оди́н (odín)
    Ordinal: пе́рвый (pérvyj)
    Ordinal abbreviation: 1-й (1-j), 1-ый (1-yj)
    Adverbial: одна́жды (odnáždy)
    Multiplier: одино́кий (odinókij)
    Collective: оди́н (odín)

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • перво́й (pervój) — archaic, obsolete

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic пьрвъ (pĭrvŭ, “first”), from Proto-Slavic *pьrvъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *pírˀwas, from Proto-Indo-European *pr̥h₂wós, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *per- (“before, formerly; through, throughout”).

Baltic cognates include Lithuanian pi̇̀rmas (“first; primary”), Latvian pìrmaĩs, Old Prussian pirmas (“first”).

Indo-European cognates include Sanskrit पूर्व (pū́rva, “foremost, first, previous”) and English fore and prime.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈpʲervɨj]
    • Audio:(file)
  • (Belarus) IPA(key): [ˈpʲervɨj]; [ˈpʲervɨ] (phonetic respelling: пе́рвы)
  • (Ukraine) IPA(key): [ˈpʲɛrʋej]
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)

Adjective

[edit]

пе́рвый • (pérvyj) (comparative (по)пе́рвее or (по)пе́рвей, superlative (наи)перве́йший, adverb во-пе́рвых or впервы́е or на́перво or пе́рво-на́перво or по́перву or сперва́, abstract noun (used in по пе́рвости (po pérvosti), else occasional) пе́рвость)

  1. first
    пе́рвый день неде́ли ― pérvyj denʹ nedéli ― the first day of the week
  2. chief, main
  3. number one, top

  • пе́рвый блин ко́мом (pérvyj blin kómom)
